findings.reason: extend the gate's `suite_command` owner (or derive one key from the other) rather than fork the project's suite command into a parallel `review.suite.command`.
findings.text: §6's `review.suite.command` is a second declaration of the project's test-suite command beside the existing `gates.suite_command` (`GateConfig.suite_command`, read at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7182` and validated against run suite arming at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:5806`), so a project declares its suite in two places and the two can drift

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/review_tiers.py` hides the three-tier precedence and the unreadable/over-ceiling fallback behind `review_tier()`, and `reckon/crew/standing_suite.py` hides run, record, hold and waiver behind four functions; both land behind interfaces smaller than the behaviour they carry.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 declares the project test-suite command a second time under `review.suite.command` beside the gate's existing `gates.suite_command`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 adds a project standing-suite subsystem and a new `review.suite` flight block with no prior-art search, where §2 cites `s25-reuse-map-review-and-velocity/reuse-map.md` and §5 cites `s25-reuse-map-review-reflex/reuse-map.md` for §3–§5.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the new modules add decision logic (tier precedence, collection-failure decided from evidence) rather than forwarding to existing machinery, and §5's reviewed-head resolution consolidated onto one `_run_head_for_review` helper instead of a spread of per-caller wrappers.
